344	    /// Each regular file under `paths` cloned from `source` to `destination`
345	    /// (`copyfile` with `COPYFILE_CLONE`, which falls back to a copy where
346	    /// the volume cannot clone), folders created; throws on the first
347	    /// failure, naming the file. Main.
348	    static func copy(_ paths: [String], from source: URL, to destination: URL) throws -> Report {
349	        let began = Date()
350	        let files = FileManager.default
351	        var count = 0
352	        var bytes: Int64 = 0
353	        func clone(_ relative: String) throws {
354	            let from = source.appendingPathComponent(relative)
355	            let to = destination.appendingPathComponent(relative)
356	            try files.createDirectory(
357	                at: to.deletingLastPathComponent(), withIntermediateDirectories: true)
358	            guard copyfile(from.path, to.path, nil, copyfile_flags_t(COPYFILE_CLONE)) == 0 else {
359	                let why = String(cString: strerror(errno))
360	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "cache/\(relative) could not be carried: \(why)")
361	            }
362	            count += 1
363	            let size = (try? files.attributesOfItem(atPath: to.path)[.size] as? NSNumber)
364	            bytes += size?.int64Value ?? 0
365	        }
366	        for relative in paths {
367	            var isFolder: ObjCBool = false
368	            let from = source.appendingPathComponent(relative)
369	            guard files.fileExists(atPath: from.path, isDirectory: &isFolder) else { continue }
370	            guard isFolder.boolValue else {
371	                try clone(relative)
372	                continue
373	            }
374	            try files.createDirectory(
375	                at: destination.appendingPathComponent(relative), withIntermediateDirectories: true)
376	            for inner in try regularFiles(under: from) { try clone("\(relative)/\(inner)") }
377	        }
378	        return Report(files: count, bytes: bytes, seconds: Date().timeIntervalSince(began))
379	    }

424	    static func carryGraphics(names: Set<String>, from folder: URL, into store: GraphicStore) throws {
425	        let files = FileManager.default

427	            let module = folder.appendingPathComponent(name + ".js")
428	            guard files.fileExists(atPath: module.path) else { continue }
429	            try store.write(name: name, bytes: try Data(contentsOf: module))
430	        }

434	                var isFolder: ObjCBool = false

436	                guard files.fileExists(atPath: file.path, isDirectory: &isFolder),
437	                    !isFolder.boolValue
438	                else { continue }

445	/// Every piece's SOURCE clip: a second half maps to the clip its original
446	/// was cut from, so a piece cut twice still names the clip a person saw.
447	/// An uncut clip, absent from the map, is its own source.
448	struct Pieces(HashMap<u32, u32>);
449	
450	impl Pieces {
451	    fn source(&self, piece: u32) -> u32 {
452	        self.0.get(&piece).copied().unwrap_or(piece)
453	    }

455	    /// The pieces of `source` in `project` satisfying `which`.
456	    fn of(&self, project: &Project, source: u32, which: impl Fn(&Clip) -> bool) -> Vec<u32> {
457	        project
458	            .clips
459	            .iter()
460	            .filter(|c| self.source(c.id) == source && which(c))
461	            .map(|c| c.id)
462	            .collect()

466	impl Project {
467	    /// The project holding only `[from, to)` of its top-level timeline,
468	    /// moved to start at 0 (spec §11 CJ-50; the module doc is the rule).
469	    pub fn keep_range(&self, from: Ticks, to: Ticks) -> Result<Outcome, String> {
470	        let from = self.snapped(from).max(0);
471	        let to = self.snapped(to).max(0);
472	        if to <= from {
473	            return Err(format!(
474	                "keep_range's to must be after its from (from {from}, to {to} ticks, on the frame \
475	                 grid)"
476	            ));
477	        }
478	
479	        // (b) Before anything is cut: a nest clip across either edge.
480	        for bound in [from, to] {
481	            if let Some(nest) = self
482	                .clips
483	                .iter()
484	                .find(|c| nest_of(c).is_some() && c.start < bound && bound < clip_end(c))
485	            {
486	                return Ok(Outcome::Refused(format!(
487	                    "Clip {} is a nest across the range's edge; a nest clip has no in point, so a \
488	                     cut there would replay it from its start. Move the edge, or open the nest \
489	                     and unnest it.",
490	                    nest.id
491	                )));
492	            }
493	        }
494	
495	        // (c) Both bounds cut on every track, locked or not.
496	        let mut next = self.clone();
497	        let mut pieces = Pieces(HashMap::new());
498	        for bound in [from, to] {
499	            let ids: Vec<u32> = next
500	                .clips
501	                .iter()
502	                .filter(|c| c.start < bound && bound < clip_end(c))
503	                .map(|c| c.id)
504	                .collect();
505	            let mut halves: Vec<(u32, u32)> = Vec::new();
506	            for id in ids {
507	                // `split_clip` allocates the second half's id first.
508	                let second = next.next_id;
509	                if split_clip(&mut next, id, bound) {
510	                    let source = pieces.source(id);
511	                    pieces.0.insert(second, source);
512	                    halves.push((id, second));
513	                }
514	            }
515	            pair_split_halves(&mut next, &halves);
516	        }
517	
518	        // (d) THE overlap rule at the edges, on the source's overlaps.
519	        let mut dropped: HashSet<u32> = HashSet::new();
520	        let mut hard_start: HashSet<u32> = HashSet::new();
521	        for track in &self.tracks {
522	            for overlap in self.overlaps_on_track(track.id) {
523	                let os = overlap.start;
524	                let oe = overlap.start.saturating_add(overlap.duration);
525	                if os <= from && from < oe {
526	                    dropped.extend(pieces.of(&next, overlap.earlier, |c| c.start == from));
527	                    hard_start.extend(pieces.of(&next, overlap.later, |c| c.start == from));
528	                }
529	                if os < to && to <= oe {
530	                    // A piece starting at `from` is the incoming piece the
531	                    // `from` rule just kept: both bounds lie in this one
532	                    // overlap, and it stays, hard-cut.
533	                    dropped.extend(pieces.of(&next, overlap.later, |c| {
534	                        clip_end(c) == to && c.start != from
535	                    }));
536	                }
537	            }
538	        }
539	
540	        // (e) Keep what lies wholly inside, and move it to 0.
541	        next.clips
542	            .retain(|c| !dropped.contains(&c.id) && c.start >= from && clip_end(c) <= to);
543	        for clip in &mut next.clips {
544	            clip.start = clip.start.saturating_sub(from);
545	            if hard_start.contains(&clip.id) {
546	                clip.transition_in = None;
547	            }
548	        }
549	        next.markers.retain(|m| from <= m.time && m.time < to);
550	        for marker in &mut next.markers {
551	            marker.time = marker.time.saturating_sub(from);
552	        }
553	
554	        // (f) What the kept timeline no longer reaches.
555	        prune_unused(&mut next);
556	
557	        // (g) Refusals on what is left.
558	        if next.clips.is_empty() {
559	            return Ok(Outcome::Refused(format!(
560	                "Nothing plays between {from} and {to} ticks."
561	            )));
562	        }
563	        for track in &next.tracks {
564	            let Err(why) = next.check_overlap_rule(&[], track.id, &[]) else {
565	                continue;
566	            };
567	            let too_long = next.overlaps_on_track(track.id).into_iter().find(|o| {
568	                match (next.clip(o.earlier), next.clip(o.later)) {
569	                    (Some(a), Some(b)) => o.duration > overlap_limit(a, b),
570	                    _ => false,
571	                }
572	            });
573	            let Some(overlap) = too_long else {
574	                return Ok(Outcome::Refused(why));
575	            };
576	            let limit = match (next.clip(overlap.earlier), next.clip(overlap.later)) {
577	                (Some(a), Some(b)) => overlap_limit(a, b),
578	                _ => 0,
579	            };
580	            return Ok(Outcome::Refused(format!(
581	                "Keeping {from} to {to} ticks would leave clips {} and {} overlapping by {} \
582	                 ticks, more than half of the shorter piece ({limit} ticks); move an edge \
583	                 further from their transition.",
584	                pieces.source(overlap.earlier),
585	                pieces.source(overlap.later),
586	                overlap.duration
587	            )));
588	        }
589	        self.finish(next)
590	    }
591	}

602	        }

605	        }

611	        .clips
612	        .iter()
613	        .chain(project.nests.iter().flat_map(|n| n.clips.iter()));

1	# Projects and media
2	
3	A Frame Job project is a `.framejob` package: one file in the Finder that holds the edit, the caches that make it quick to reopen, and, when you ask for it, copies of the footage itself. This page covers starting a project (most often by opening a movie), saving it, what is inside the package, the canvas settings on the Document tab, bringing files in, the Media tab, and what to do when files go missing.
4	
5	## Starting a project
6	
7	### Open a movie
8	
9	The quickest way in is to open the footage itself. **File ▸ Open…** (⌘O) on a movie, **Open With ▸ Frame Job** in the Finder (or a double-click, once Frame Job is that file type's default app), a drop on the Dock icon, or a drop onto a Frame Job window all do the same thing:
10	
11	- an **untitled** project is created, sized and rated to the file;
12	- the file becomes the first media item and the first clip on Track 1, starting at 0;
13	- the window is titled after the movie (`Interview.mov` opens as "Interview").
14	
15	The canvas takes the movie's *display* size, so a portrait phone clip opens as 1080 × 1920, not sideways. Its frame rate is read exactly: a 29.97 or 23.976 file stays 29.97 or 23.976, not 30 or 24.
16	
17	Opening a sound file works the same way, but a sound file has no picture: its project is 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps. Opening a picture (PNG, JPEG, HEIC) makes a project at the picture's pixel size, 30 fps, with the picture as a 5-second clip.
18	
19	The new project lives only in memory until you save it, so it opens already marked as changed. Closing it asks whether to save. The first **Save** offers to put the package next to the source file, under the source's name.
20	
21	Opening a `.framejob` package opens that project (a double-click on a package always opens it in Frame Job). If it is already open, its window comes forward.
22	
23	Dropping several files at once on a window, the Welcome window or the Dock icon opens each one as its own untitled project. Only `.framejob` packages and the movie, sound and picture types File ▸ Open… lists are taken; anything else dropped there is ignored. To add files to the project you already have open, drop them on the [Media tab](#the-media-tab) instead.
24	
25	*Agents:* `open_project` (takes a `path` to a package, movie, sound file or picture; answers `already_open: true` when that file is already open).
26	
27	### New Project
28	
29	**File ▸ New Project** (⌘N) opens a blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project with no dialog, in a window titled "Untitled Project". Change the size and rate afterwards on the Document tab (see [The Document tab](#the-document-tab-canvas-settings)).
30	
31	*Agents:* `new_project` (an optional `path` saves it there straight away; without one it stays an untitled draft).
32	
33	### New Project from Range
34	
35	With an In–Out range set on the timeline (Mark ▸ Set In and Set Out), **File ▸ New Project from Range…** opens a new project holding exactly that range, moved to start at 0. A clip across the range's In or Out is cut there, as **Split** cuts it; a transition across an edge becomes a hard start or end; markers inside the range are kept. Media that no kept clip plays are left out. The item is off with no range set, while a nest is open, and while a sheet is on the window.
36	
37	The new project opens untitled and with unsaved changes, named after the project it came from with " (range)" added (for example "Interview (range)"). It starts at the range: there is no undo step back to the whole timeline. The project you made it from does not change.
38	
39	What it brings with it, so nothing has to be measured again when it opens:
40	
41	- each kept media's filmstrip, waveform, loudness, speech and sync caches, the transcripts read on this Mac, its analyses (shots, people's masks, faces, sound events, subjects) and the backwards render of a reversed clip;
42	- a cloud transcript only once AssemblyAI has been told to delete its copy; one still waiting for that stays in the original project;
43	- the graphic modules its clips draw, and every font and asset of the project's graphics.
44	
45	It does not copy media files (the new project uses the same files), speed-ramp, isolated-voice or voice-effect renders (they are made again when needed), or a graphic's kept history. If the range cannot be kept — a nest clip across an edge, or nothing playing in it — the item beeps and shows why at the foot of the inspector.
46	
47	*Agents:* `new_project_from_range {from, to, path?}` (with `path`, the new project is saved there first; nothing may exist there yet).
48	
49	### The Welcome window
50	
51	When Frame Job starts with nothing to open, and when you click its Dock icon with no window open, it shows the Welcome window. It holds:
52	
53	| Control | What it does |
54	|---|---|
55	| **Open Video…** | The same open panel as File ▸ Open…. |
56	| **New Project** | A blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project. |
57	| **New Recording…** | Opens the screen recorder panel; see [Screen recording](screen-recording.md). |
58	| **Recent** | Up to five recently opened projects, by name; hover for the full path. Hidden when there are none. |
59	
60	The line at the foot lists the file types it opens: MOV · MP4 · M4V · M4A · MP3 · WAV · AIFF · PNG · JPEG · HEIC. You can also drop a file or a package anywhere on the Welcome window to open it. The window closes itself as soon as a project window comes up.
61	
62	## Saving, reverting and closing
63	## Limits
64	
65	- Consolidate Media needs a saved project.
66	- Canvas width and height are even numbers from 16 to 16384 px.
67	- A project holds at most 4,096 clips and 64 tracks (counting those inside nests), 1,024 markers and 1,024 media files, with nests up to 8 deep.
68	- The Add Media… and Open panels list movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG, HEIC and (Add Media… only) `.cube`. Other sound and picture formats import only by a drop on the Media tab, or through `import_media`.
69	- `.cube` files are imported, not opened: File ▸ Open… does not take one, and a `.cube` dropped on the window or the Dock is not imported. Use Add Media… or a drop on the Media tab.
70	- A project file that is damaged or out of range fails to open with a message naming the problem; the package is not rewritten. A package saved by a newer Frame Job reports "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it". A package with no readable `project.json` reports "*name* does not contain a readable project.json."

412	    /// `cache/` directory is regenerable and is NEVER required to open — a
413	    /// missing or damaged one costs nothing but a redrawn filmstrip.

416	    /// draw a slate, and `missingMedia` feeds the Relink… offer.
417	    private func readPackage(at url: URL) throws {
418	        let jsonURL = url.appendingPathComponent(Self.projectFileName)
419	        let wrapper = try FileWrapper(url: jsonURL, options: .immediate)
420	        guard let data = wrapper.regularFileContents,
421	              let text = String(data: data, encoding: .utf8)
422	        else {

424	                message: "\(url.lastPathComponent) does not contain a readable project.json.")
425	        }
426	        project = Self.repairingMedia(try ReelProject.from(json: text), package: url)
427	        // Four of the five pieces of view state; the fifth is `nestPath`, and
428	        // it is `read(from:ofType:)`'s `clampViewState()` rather than a line
429	        // here — that method's doc says why the scope cannot be zeroed in
430	        // this file.
431	        playhead = 0
432	        selection = []
433	        inOutRange = nil
434	        selectedMedia = nil

437	    /// Points missing media at the package's own `media/` directory when the
438	    /// file it names is in there under the same name.
439	    ///
440	    /// Consolidate stores an ABSOLUTE path (the model has no relative form —
441	    /// `Media.path` in `model.rs`), so moving or renaming a consolidated
442	    /// package would otherwise break every link inside it and hand the user
443	    /// a Relink… sheet for footage that never left the package. This is the
444	    /// repair, and it is deliberately narrow: only media that resolves to
445	    /// NOTHING is touched, so a working link is never overridden by a
446	    /// same-named file that happens to sit in `media/`.
447	    ///
448	    /// Not an edit. It runs on the read queue before the document exists as
449	    /// far as AppKit is concerned, registers no undo step and dirties
450	    /// nothing; the new paths are written out by whatever save comes next.
451	    static func reanchoringConsolidatedMedia(
452	        _ project: ReelProject, package: URL
453	    ) -> ReelProject {
454	        let directory = package.appendingPathComponent(mediaDirectoryName, isDirectory: true)
455	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: directory.path) else { return project }
456	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
457	        for media in project.snapshot.media where mediaURL(for: media) == nil {
458	            let name = (media.path as NSString).lastPathComponent
459	            guard !name.isEmpty else { continue }
460	            let candidate = directory.appendingPathComponent(name)
461	            guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) else { continue }
462	            ops.append(.relinkMedia(media: media.id, path: candidate.path))
463	        }
464	        guard !ops.isEmpty else { return project }
465	        // Only `.applied` is a repair; both other arms leave it as opened.
466	        return (try? project.applying(ops)).project ?? project
467	    }

469	    /// Spec §1's opening flow: a movie, sound file or picture becomes a fresh
470	    /// project sized and rated to it, with the file as the first clip on
471	    /// Track 1.
472	    ///
473	    /// The probe is asynchronous (`MediaImporter` is the one file allowed
474	    /// `async`/`await`) and this method is not, so it blocks on
475	    /// `MediaImporter.probeBlocking`. That call is deliberately the one face
476	    /// of the probe that never touches the main actor: this method can and
477	    /// does run ON the main thread — `canConcurrentlyReadDocuments` only
478	    /// governs NSDocumentController's asynchronous open path, and a read
479	    /// AppKit itself makes on main arrives there — so a completion delivered
480	    /// through `MainActor.run` would deadlock against its own waiter.
481	    private func readMediaFile(at url: URL) throws {
482	        let descriptor = try Self.probeForOpening(url)
483	        try adoptImported(descriptor, source: url)

486	    /// `readMediaFile`'s body once its probe has answered, and the door
487	    /// `untitled(around:)` (`ProjectDocument+Recording.swift`, which argues
488	    /// it) comes in by — ONE spelling of how a probed file becomes this
489	    /// document's project. `fps` non-nil replaces the canvas rate alone.
490	    func adoptImported(_ descriptor: MediaDescriptor, source: URL, fps: Fps? = nil) throws {
491	        // Set BEFORE the project is built: it is what makes the `fileURL` and
492	        // `fileType` overrides above refuse the assignments NSDocument makes
493	        // as soon as the read returns. Written on the read queue and read
494	        // on the main thread afterwards, which NSDocument's own hand-off
495	        // between the two orders for us.
496	        importSourceURL = source
497	        // …and undo the assignment NSDocument may already have made, on the
498	        // open path that sets the two BEFORE the read (see `fileURL` above).
499	        // A document left pointing at the movie is not untitled, and saving
500	        // it writes a package over the source file.
501	        fileURL = nil
502	        fileType = Self.projectTypeIdentifier
503	        project = try Self.makeProject(around: descriptor, fps: fps)
504	        // The same four, and the same note: `nestPath` is cleared by
505	        // `read(from:ofType:)`'s clamp. A file-import read is always a fresh
506	        // document, so the path is empty already — the line is not here
507	        // because the rule has one home, not because this path is special.
508	        playhead = 0
509	        selection = []
510	        inOutRange = nil
511	        selectedMedia = nil
512	    }

514	    /// Builds the project one imported file becomes. The canvas takes the
515	    /// source's display size and rate when it has video; an audio-only file
516	    /// has neither, so it lands on the 1080p/30 default. A non-nil `fps`
517	    /// replaces that rate and nothing else: the media record keeps the file's.
518	    private static func makeProject(
519	        around descriptor: MediaDescriptor, fps: Fps? = nil
520	    ) throws -> ReelProject {
521	        let width = descriptor.hasVideo && descriptor.width > 0 ? descriptor.width : 1920
522	        let height = descriptor.hasVideo && descriptor.height > 0 ? descriptor.height : 1080
523	        let fps =
524	            fps ?? (descriptor.hasVideo && descriptor.fps.double > 0 ? descriptor.fps : .thirty)
525	        guard let base = ReelProject.new(width: width, height: height, fps: fps) else {
526	            throw ReelCoreError(
527	                message: "\(descriptor.path) reports a size or frame rate a project cannot use.")
528	        }
529	        // Neither non-applied arm is reachable on a fresh project, and one
530	        // that answered with the project unchanged would be worse than this.
531	        guard let withMedia = try base.applying(.addMedia(descriptor: descriptor)).project else {
532	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "The file could not be added to a project.")
533	        }
534	        // `add_media` returns a project, not an id (there is one FFI entry
535	        // point for every op, §11), so the id is read back off the new
536	        // snapshot: the core appends, so the last entry is the new one.
537	        let snapshot = withMedia.snapshot
538	        guard let media = snapshot.media.last, let track = snapshot.tracks.first else {
539	            return withMedia
540	        }
541	        // A clip the core refuses (an empty media, say) is not fatal, and
542	        // neither is an identity or a throw: all three open the project with
543	        // the file in the Media tab, which is better than not opening it.
544	        return (try? withMedia.applying(.addClip(track: track.id, media: media.id, at: 0)))
545	            .project ?? withMedia
546	    }

550	    /// The package: `project.json` written by the CORE (nothing re-encodes a
551	    /// `ProjectSnapshot` — the core owns the file format) plus the
552	    /// regenerable `cache/` directory, carried across so a save does not
553	    /// throw away every filmstrip.
554	    override func fileWrapper(ofType typeName: String) throws -> FileWrapper {
555	        guard let data = project.json.data(using: .utf8) else {
556	            throw ReelCoreError(message: "The project could not be encoded.")
557	        }
558	        let json = FileWrapper(regularFileWithContents: data)
559	        json.preferredFilename = Self.projectFileName
560	        var children = [Self.projectFileName: json]
561	        if let cache = cacheWrapper() { children[Self.cacheDirectoryName] = cache }
562	        // Consolidated media, carried across the same way — and it is not
563	        // optional the way the cache is: this wrapper is a whitelist, so a
564	        // `media/` left out here is a `media/` DELETED by the next save
565	        // (autosave included), taking the only copy of the footage with it.
566	        if let media = directoryWrapper(Self.mediaDirectoryName) {
567	            children[Self.mediaDirectoryName] = media
568	        }
569	        if let graphics = graphicsWrapper() { children[Self.graphicsDirectoryName] = graphics }
570	        return FileWrapper(directoryWithFileWrappers: children)
571	    }

149	    /// The rates a container is allowed to round: the integer rates and the
150	    /// three NTSC /1001 rates (§7.7). Anything else keeps three decimals as
151	    /// `[round(fps × 1000), 1000]`, which is exact enough to place source
152	    /// frames and never pretends a 47.3 fps screen recording is 48.
153	    static let commonRates: [Fps] = [
154	        Fps(num: 24, den: 1), Fps(num: 24000, den: 1001), Fps(num: 25, den: 1),
155	        Fps(num: 30, den: 1), Fps(num: 30000, den: 1001), Fps(num: 48, den: 1),
156	        Fps(num: 50, den: 1), Fps(num: 60, den: 1), Fps(num: 60000, den: 1001),
157	    ]
158	
159	    /// Tolerance for that match, in frames per second. 0.01 is wide enough
160	    /// for a float's error at 60 fps and narrower than the 0.03 gap between
161	    /// 29.97 and 30 — the pair this must never confuse.
162	    static let rateTolerance = 0.01
163	
164	    static func rationalFrameRate(_ nominal: Double) -> Fps {
165	        guard nominal.isFinite, nominal > 0 else { return .thirty }
166	        for candidate in commonRates where abs(candidate.double - nominal) <= rateTolerance {
167	            return candidate
168	        }
169	        return Fps(num: Int((nominal * 1000).rounded()), den: 1000)
170	    }

344	    /// Each regular file under `paths` cloned from `source` to `destination`
345	    /// (`copyfile` with `COPYFILE_CLONE`, which falls back to a copy where
346	    /// the volume cannot clone), folders created; throws on the first
347	    /// failure, naming the file. Main.
348	    static func copy(_ paths: [String], from source: URL, to destination: URL) throws -> Report {
349	        let began = Date()
350	        let files = FileManager.default
351	        var count = 0
352	        var bytes: Int64 = 0
353	        func clone(_ relative: String) throws {
354	            let from = source.appendingPathComponent(relative)
355	            let to = destination.appendingPathComponent(relative)
356	            try files.createDirectory(
357	                at: to.deletingLastPathComponent(), withIntermediateDirectories: true)
358	            guard copyfile(from.path, to.path, nil, copyfile_flags_t(COPYFILE_CLONE)) == 0 else {
359	                let why = String(cString: strerror(errno))
360	                throw ReelCoreError(message: "cache/\(relative) could not be carried: \(why)")
361	            }
362	            count += 1
363	            let size = (try? files.attributesOfItem(atPath: to.path)[.size] as? NSNumber)
364	            bytes += size?.int64Value ?? 0
365	        }
366	        for relative in paths {
367	            var isFolder: ObjCBool = false
368	            let from = source.appendingPathComponent(relative)
369	            guard files.fileExists(atPath: from.path, isDirectory: &isFolder) else { continue }
370	            guard isFolder.boolValue else {
371	                try clone(relative)
372	                continue
373	            }
374	            try files.createDirectory(
375	                at: destination.appendingPathComponent(relative), withIntermediateDirectories: true)
376	            for inner in try regularFiles(under: from) { try clone("\(relative)/\(inner)") }
377	        }

379	    }

open_project Opens a project and shows its window. Takes a .framejob package, or any movie, sound file or picture — opening one of those builds a fresh UNTITLED project sized and rated to it with the file as the first clip on track 1, exactly as double-clicking it does. Answers already_open: true when that file is already open.
new_project Creates a blank 1920×1080 / 30 fps project and shows its window — File ▸ New Project. With path it is saved there straight away (a .framejob extension is added if missing) so later calls can name it; without one it stays an untitled draft until save_project. Change the size and rate afterwards with set_canvas. A path another open project holds is refused, and nothing is created; close_project closes that one first.
new_project_from_range Opens a NEW project holding exactly [from, to) of the top-level timeline, moved to start at 0 — what File ▸ New Project from Range… does with the In–Out range. Times are TIMELINE ticks (600000 per second), snapped to frames. A clip across an edge is cut there as split cuts it; a transition across an edge becomes a hard start or end; markers inside are kept; media no kept clip plays are left out. Each kept media's caches (filmstrips, waveforms, loudness, speech, sync, transcripts read on this Mac, the media analysis, reversed renders) and the graphic modules the kept clips draw, with every font and asset, are carried, so nothing is re-analysed; media files are never copied (the new project points at the same files), and a cloud transcript still owed a deletion stays behind. The project you name never changes and gets no undo step. Without path the new project opens untitled, with unsaved changes, named "<name> (range)"; with path it is saved there first. Refused while a nest is open, onto a path another open project holds or where anything already exists, and in the core's own sentence for a nest clip across an edge or a range where nothing plays. Answers {project, saved (with path), carried {files, bytes, seconds}}; name the new project by its path or name in later calls.

open_project Opens a project and shows its window. Takes a .framejob package, or any movie, sound file or picture — opening one of those builds a fresh UNTITLED project sized and rated to it with the file as the first clip on track 1, exactly as double-clicking it does. Answers already_open: true when that file is already open.
new_project Creates a blank 1920×1080 / 30 fps project and shows its window — File ▸ New Project. With path it is saved there straight away (a .framejob extension is added if missing) so later calls can name it; without one it stays an untitled draft until save_project. Change the size and rate afterwards with set_canvas. A path another open project holds is refused, and nothing is created; close_project closes that one first.
new_project_from_range Opens a NEW project holding exactly [from, to) of the top-level timeline, moved to start at 0 — what File ▸ New Project from Range… does with the In–Out range. Times are TIMELINE ticks (600000 per second), snapped to frames. A clip across an edge is cut there as split cuts it; a transition across an edge becomes a hard start or end; markers inside are kept; media no kept clip plays are left out. Each kept media's caches (filmstrips, waveforms, loudness, speech, sync, transcripts read on this Mac, the media analysis, reversed renders) and the graphic modules the kept clips draw, with every font and asset, are carried, so nothing is re-analysed; media files are never copied (the new project points at the same files), and a cloud transcript still owed a deletion stays behind. The project you name never changes and gets no undo step. Without path the new project opens untitled, with unsaved changes, named "<name> (range)"; with path it is saved there first. Refused while a nest is open, onto a path another open project holds or where anything already exists, and in the core's own sentence for a nest clip across an edge or a range where nothing plays. Answers {project, saved (with path), carried {files, bytes, seconds}}; name the new project by its path or name in later calls.

---
title: Start a project
description: Open a movie, sound file or picture as a new project sized to it, or start from a blank one, and see where the first save goes.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The quickest way in is to open the footage itself. Frame Job builds a project around the file, at its size and frame rate, with the file already on the timeline. If you'd rather start empty, **New Project** gives you a blank one. To open a project you've already saved, see [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ New Project']}
  keys={['⌘O', '⌘N']}
  where={['Welcome window ▸ Open Video…', 'Welcome window ▸ New Project', 'Finder ▸ Open With ▸ Frame Job']}
  tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'import_media', 'save_project']}
/>

## Open a movie

Any of these does the same thing:

- Choose **File ▸ Open…** (<kbd>⌘O</kbd>), or **Open Video…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/), and pick the file.
- In the Finder, choose **Open With ▸ Frame Job**.
- Double-click the file, once you've made Frame Job the default app for that file type.
- [Drop the file](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them) on the Dock icon or on a Frame Job window.

Frame Job appears under **Open With** for movies and for M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files, but it doesn't take over their double-click unless you make it the default.

You get an untitled project with the movie as its first media file and its first clip, at the very start of Track 1. The window is named after the file, so `Interview.mov` opens as "Interview".

A WebM or MKV file is [copied into a movie](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) first. A file macOS can't open may still come in [through ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), if you have it installed.

## Open a sound file

Open a sound file the same way. A sound file has no picture to take a size from, so its project is 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, with the sound as the first clip on Track 1. A movie file that holds only sound gets the same project.

## Open a picture

Open a PNG, JPEG or HEIC the same way. The project takes the picture's pixel size, runs at 30 fps, and holds the picture as a 5-second clip on Track 1.

## The size and rate you get

| You open | Canvas size | Frame rate | First clip |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A movie | The size it displays at | The file's exact rate | The whole movie |
| A sound file | 1920 × 1080 | 30 fps | The whole sound |
| A picture | Its pixel size | 30 fps | 5 seconds of the picture |

### Display size

A project built from a movie uses the size the movie displays at, after the file's rotation. A portrait phone clip opens as 1080 × 1920, not sideways.

An odd-sized movie keeps its size, even though a canvas size you type must be even. Once you change either canvas field, both sides have to be even. See [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/).

### Exact frame rate

The rate is read from the file and never rounded to a neighbour, so 29.97 stays 29.97 and 23.976 stays 23.976.

A file's rate is matched to a standard rate if it's within 0.01 fps of one: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60. Any other rate is kept to three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48. A movie that reports no usable rate opens at 30 fps.

Every file you [add to a project](/projects/import-media/) is read the same way. To change the project's rate later, see [Project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/).

## Start a blank project

Choose **File ▸ New Project** (<kbd>⌘N</kbd>), or **New Project** on the Welcome window. A blank project opens at once, with no dialog, in a window titled "Untitled Project". It's 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, with one empty track.

**New Project** is always available, whether or not another project is open. Change the size and rate afterwards on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).

## Save it for the first time

A project made from a file exists only in its window until you save it. It opens already marked as changed, so closing it asks whether to save, even if you've done nothing to it yet.

The first **File ▸ Save** (<kbd>⌘S</kbd>) offers to put the project next to the source file, under the source's name: the save panel opens in that file's folder, with the file's name and no extension. `Interview.mov` becomes `Interview.framejob` beside it, unless you choose otherwise.

Saving never writes over the source file. A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. See [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/).

## With an agent

`new_project` can save the blank project at a path straight away, adding `.framejob` if the path lacks it. It won't use a path another open project holds, or one a window is still opening, and then nothing is created. Without a path the project stays an untitled draft. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

## Related

- [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/)
- [The Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/)
- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
- [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/)

---
title: The Welcome window
description: Use the window Frame Job shows when nothing is open to open a file, start a project or a recording, or reopen something recent.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Welcome window is where you start when no project is open. It offers the ways in and your recent projects, and it takes dropped files.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Shown when Frame Job starts with nothing to open', 'Shown when you click the Dock icon with no window open']}
  tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'record_screen']}
/>

<Shot
  name="01-welcome.window"
  alt="The Welcome window: the Frame Job mark and name, the line Open a file. Start cutting., a note about what opening a movie does, the buttons Open Video…, New Project and New Recording…, and a line of file types at the foot."
/>

## Start something

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Open Video…** | Shows the same open panel as **File ▸ Open…**. A movie becomes an untitled project at its own size and rate, with the file as the first clip on Track 1. Despite the name it also opens sound files, pictures and saved `.framejob` projects. |
| **New Project** | Starts a blank 1920 × 1080, 30 fps project. |
| **New Recording…** | Opens the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), with no project needed. |

**New Recording…** never stops a recording, unlike the **File** menu item, which reads **Stop Recording** while one runs. If you press it during a recording, it beeps.

For what you get from each, see [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/).

## Reopen a recent project

Under the buttons, **Recent** lists up to five recently opened projects by name, most recent first. Click one to reopen it. Hover over a row to see its full path.

The heading and the list disappear when there's nothing recent. [**File ▸ Open Recent**](/projects/open-a-project/#open-a-recent-project) keeps the same list, so **Clear Menu** empties this one too.

## Drop files on it

Drag a file or a project from the Finder and drop it anywhere on the window. Each file opens as its own document, so several files make several projects.

The window takes `.framejob` projects and the movie, sound and picture types **File ▸ Open…** lists, and ignores anything else. The line at the foot of the window names the common ones: MOV · MP4 · M4V · M4A · MP3 · WAV · AIFF · PNG · JPEG · HEIC.

## When it appears and goes away

Frame Job shows the Welcome window when it starts with nothing to open, and when you click its Dock icon with no window open. It closes itself as soon as a project window comes up.

Closing the last project doesn't bring it back on its own, and Frame Job keeps running. Click the Dock icon to see it again.

The window is a fixed 720 × 600 and can't be resized.

## Related

- [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/)
- [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/)
- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)

---
title: Open a project
description: Open a saved .framejob project from the File menu, the Finder or a drop, and see what happens with older, newer, damaged or incomplete projects.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A project is a `.framejob` package: one item in the Finder that holds your edit. This page is about opening one you've saved. To turn a movie, sound file or picture into a new project, see [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ Open Recent ▸', 'File ▸ Open Recent ▸ Clear Menu']}
  keys="⌘O"
  where={['Double-click in the Finder', 'Welcome window ▸ Open Video…', 'Welcome window ▸ Recent', 'A drop on the Dock icon or a window']}
  tools={['open_project', 'relink_media']}
/>

## Open a saved project

Choose **File ▸ Open…** (<kbd>⌘O</kbd>) and pick the package, or double-click it in the Finder. A double-click on a `.framejob` always opens it in Frame Job.

The open panel lists projects along with QuickTime, MPEG-4 and M4V files, other movies, and M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files. Everything but a project opens as a [fresh untitled project](/projects/start-a-project/).

A `.fjgraphic` isn't a project, and **File ▸ Open…** doesn't list one. See [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).

## Open a recent project

**File ▸ Open Recent ▸** lists the projects you've opened lately. macOS fills the list. **Clear Menu** at the foot of it empties it.

The [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/#reopen-a-recent-project) shows the five most recent from the same list.

## Drop files to open them

Drag from the Finder onto a project window, the Welcome window or the Dock icon. Each file opens as a document of its own:

- A `.framejob` package opens that project.
- A media file opens as a fresh untitled project built around it, so several files make several projects.

Only projects and the types **File ▸ Open…** lists are taken: MOV, MP4, M4V and other movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC. Anything else is ignored.

:::caution
A drop on a project window doesn't add to that project. To add a file to the project you have open, drop it on the [Media tab](/projects/import-media/). Anywhere else in the window, the timeline and preview included, the drop opens a new project.
:::

## Open a project that's already open

Opening a saved project that's already open brings its window forward. It doesn't open a second copy.

That's for saved projects. A movie opened as an untitled project has no file of its own yet, so opening the same movie again makes a second untitled project.

## Open a project from another version

A project saved by any earlier version of Frame Job opens. It's brought up to the current format as it opens, one format at a time, and the next save writes it in the current format.

A project saved by a newer Frame Job won't open. The message gives both versions and asks you to update:

> project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it

## When a project won't open

A damaged project, or one holding values out of range, fails to open with a message naming the problem. The package isn't rewritten, so a failed open costs you nothing.

| The message says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." | The edit file inside the package can't be read as text. |
| "project json is not valid json: …" | The edit file is damaged. |
| "project json does not match the schema: …" | The edit file holds something Frame Job can't read as a project. |

Filmstrips, waveforms and the like inside the package are never needed to open it. A missing or damaged one is made again. See [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).

## Open a project with missing files

A project always opens, even if its files have moved. The clips stay where they are and draw a slate in place of the picture, the project keeps their time, and the **Relink** sheet appears once, when the window first opens. You can close it and go on working, and use **Relink…** on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) later.

A project with [consolidated media](/projects/consolidate-media/) finds the copies in its own package again after the package moves, with nothing for you to do.

See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).

## With an agent

`open_project` takes a path, absolute or starting with `~`, to a project, movie, sound file or picture. It differs from a person's open in two ways:

- It also recognises a movie already open as an untitled project, and brings that window forward instead of making a second one.
- It never asks the [ffmpeg question](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).

See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

## Related

- [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/)
- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
- [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/)

**File ▸ Open Recent ▸** lists the projects you've opened lately. macOS fills the list. **Clear Menu** at the foot of it empties it.

The [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/#reopen-a-recent-project) shows the five most recent from the same list.

## Drop files to open them

Drag from the Finder onto a project window, the Welcome window or the Dock icon. Each file opens as a document of its own:

- A `.framejob` package opens that project.
- A media file opens as a fresh untitled project built around it, so several files make several projects.

Only projects and the types **File ▸ Open…** lists are taken: MOV, MP4, M4V and other movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC. Anything else is ignored.

:::caution
A drop on a project window doesn't add to that project. To add a file to the project you have open, drop it on the [Media tab](/projects/import-media/). Anywhere else in the window, the timeline and preview included, the drop opens a new project.
:::

## Open a project that's already open

Opening a saved project that's already open brings its window forward. It doesn't open a second copy.

That's for saved projects. A movie opened as an untitled project has no file of its own yet, so opening the same movie again makes a second untitled project.

## Open a project from another version

A project saved by any earlier version of Frame Job opens. It's brought up to the current format as it opens, one format at a time, and the next save writes it in the current format.

A project saved by a newer Frame Job won't open. The message gives both versions and asks you to update:

> project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it

## When a project won't open

A damaged project, or one holding values out of range, fails to open with a message naming the problem. The package isn't rewritten, so a failed open costs you nothing.

| The message says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "*name* does not contain a readable project.json." | The edit file inside the package can't be read as text. |
| "project json is not valid json: …" | The edit file is damaged. |
| "project json does not match the schema: …" | The edit file holds something Frame Job can't read as a project. |

Filmstrips, waveforms and the like inside the package are never needed to open it. A missing or damaged one is made again. See [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/).

## Open a project with missing files

A project always opens, even if its files have moved. The clips stay where they are and draw a slate in place of the picture, the project keeps their time, and the **Relink** sheet appears once, when the window first opens. You can close it and go on working, and use **Relink…** on the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) later.

A project with [consolidated media](/projects/consolidate-media/) finds the copies in its own package again after the package moves, with nothing for you to do.

See [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).

## With an agent

`open_project` takes a path, absolute or starting with `~`, to a project, movie, sound file or picture. It differs from a person's open in two ways:

- It also recognises a movie already open as an untitled project, and brings that window forward instead of making a second one.
- It never asks the [ffmpeg question](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).

See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)
- [Troubleshooting](/reference/troubleshooting/)

---
title: New Project from Range
description: Keep one stretch of your timeline as a new project of its own, with its caches and graphics, and leave the original as it is.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

New Project from Range opens a new project holding exactly the timeline's In–Out range, moved to start at 0. Use it to lift a section out of a long edit to work on by itself. The project you made it from doesn't change.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ New Project from Range…" tools="new_project_from_range" />

## Make a project from a range

<Steps>

1. Set the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) with **Mark ▸ Set In** (<kbd>I</kbd>) and **Mark ▸ Set Out** (<kbd>O</kbd>).

2. Choose **File ▸ New Project from Range…**.

</Steps>

The new project opens in its own window straight away. There's no sheet to fill in, and the command has no key.

The item is off when no range is set, while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, and while a sheet is on the window.

## What is kept

- **Clips across an edge** are cut there, the same way [Split](/editing/splitting/) cuts them. This happens on every track, locked or not, and a linked pair stays linked.
- **Clips wholly inside the range** are kept. Everything outside it goes.
- **A transition across an edge** becomes a hard start or end. The piece beyond the edge is dropped, and at the In edge the incoming piece starts with no transition.
- **Markers inside the range** are kept and moved with the timeline. A marker exactly on the Out frame isn't kept.
- **Tracks and the canvas** stay as they are, including any track that ends up empty and any lock.
- **Media no kept clip plays** is left out, unless a kept clip still needs it as a look's [LUT](/color/luts/). Nests no kept clip reaches are left out too.

## What comes with it

The new project brings what's already been measured, so nothing is measured again when it opens. For each media file it keeps:

- filmstrips, waveforms, and loudness, speech and sync data
- transcripts read on this Mac
- [analyses](/projects/media-analysis/), such as shots, people's masks, faces, sound events and subjects
- the backwards render of a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/)

Media files themselves are never copied. The new project points at the same files as the original.

[Speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), [isolated voice](/audio/voice-isolation/) and [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) renders don't come along. They're made again when needed.

### Cloud transcripts

A transcript from [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) goes to the new project only once AssemblyAI has been told to delete its copy. One still waiting for that delete stays in the original project.

### Graphics

The graphics the kept clips draw come along, and so does every font and picture of the project's graphics, whether a kept clip uses it or not. A graphic's kept earlier versions don't.

## The new project's name and undo

The new project opens untitled with unsaved changes, named after its parent with " (range)" added, such as "Interview (range)". Closing it asks whether to save.

It starts at the range. There's no undo step back to the whole timeline, and the original project gets no undo step either, because nothing happened to it.

## When Frame Job won't do it

If the range can't be kept, the command beeps and shows why at the foot of the inspector, and no project opens.

| The message says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "Clip *N* is a nest across the range's edge; a nest clip has no in point, so a cut there would replay it from its start. Move the edge, or open the nest and unnest it." | Do one of those. A nest clip can't be cut at an edge. |
| "Nothing plays between …" | The range holds no clips. Move it over something. |
| A sentence naming two clips, ending "move an edge further from their transition." | An edge would cut a clip too short for a transition inside the range, leaving them overlapping by more than half of the shorter piece. Move the edge. |

The command also beeps when In and Out are on the same frame, because the range is empty.

## With an agent

`new_project_from_range` takes the range as times, so it doesn't need the In–Out range set. It can also save the new project at a path first, as long as nothing exists there and no other open project holds it. The assistant asks you before it does that. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

## Related

- [The in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/)
- [Split clips](/editing/splitting/)
- [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/)
- [Make Vertical Version](/reframe/make-vertical/)

---
title: Start a project
description: Open a movie, sound file or picture as a new project sized to it, or start from a blank one, and see where the first save goes.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

The quickest way in is to open the footage itself. Frame Job builds a project around the file, at its size and frame rate, with the file already on the timeline. If you'd rather start empty, **New Project** gives you a blank one. To open a project you've already saved, see [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Open…', 'File ▸ New Project']}
  keys={['⌘O', '⌘N']}
  where={['Welcome window ▸ Open Video…', 'Welcome window ▸ New Project', 'Finder ▸ Open With ▸ Frame Job']}
  tools={['open_project', 'new_project', 'import_media', 'save_project']}
/>

## Open a movie

Any of these does the same thing:

- Choose **File ▸ Open…** (<kbd>⌘O</kbd>), or **Open Video…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/), and pick the file.
- In the Finder, choose **Open With ▸ Frame Job**.
- Double-click the file, once you've made Frame Job the default app for that file type.
- [Drop the file](/projects/open-a-project/#drop-files-to-open-them) on the Dock icon or on a Frame Job window.

Frame Job appears under **Open With** for movies and for M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG and HEIC files, but it doesn't take over their double-click unless you make it the default.

You get an untitled project with the movie as its first media file and its first clip, at the very start of Track 1. The window is named after the file, so `Interview.mov` opens as "Interview".

A WebM or MKV file is [copied into a movie](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) first. A file macOS can't open may still come in [through ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/), if you have it installed.

## Open a sound file

Open a sound file the same way. A sound file has no picture to take a size from, so its project is 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, with the sound as the first clip on Track 1. A movie file that holds only sound gets the same project.

## Open a picture

Open a PNG, JPEG or HEIC the same way. The project takes the picture's pixel size, runs at 30 fps, and holds the picture as a 5-second clip on Track 1.

## The size and rate you get

| You open | Canvas size | Frame rate | First clip |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A movie | The size it displays at | The file's exact rate | The whole movie |
| A sound file | 1920 × 1080 | 30 fps | The whole sound |
| A picture | Its pixel size | 30 fps | 5 seconds of the picture |

### Display size

A project built from a movie uses the size the movie displays at, after the file's rotation. A portrait phone clip opens as 1080 × 1920, not sideways.

An odd-sized movie keeps its size, even though a canvas size you type must be even. Once you change either canvas field, both sides have to be even. See [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/).

### Exact frame rate

The rate is read from the file and never rounded to a neighbour, so 29.97 stays 29.97 and 23.976 stays 23.976.

A file's rate is matched to a standard rate if it's within 0.01 fps of one: 23.976, 24, 25, 29.97, 30, 48, 50, 59.94 or 60. Any other rate is kept to three decimals, so a 47.3 fps screen recording isn't called 48. A movie that reports no usable rate opens at 30 fps.

Every file you [add to a project](/projects/import-media/) is read the same way. To change the project's rate later, see [Project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/).

## Start a blank project

Choose **File ▸ New Project** (<kbd>⌘N</kbd>), or **New Project** on the Welcome window. A blank project opens at once, with no dialog, in a window titled "Untitled Project". It's 1920 × 1080 at 30 fps, with one empty track.

**New Project** is always available, whether or not another project is open. Change the size and rate afterwards on the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/).

## Save it for the first time

A project made from a file exists only in its window until you save it. It opens already marked as changed, so closing it asks whether to save, even if you've done nothing to it yet.

The first **File ▸ Save** (<kbd>⌘S</kbd>) offers to put the project next to the source file, under the source's name: the save panel opens in that file's folder, with the file's name and no extension. `Interview.mov` becomes `Interview.framejob` beside it, unless you choose otherwise.

Saving never writes over the source file. A project only ever saves as a `.framejob` package. See [Save, revert and close](/projects/save-and-revert/).

## With an agent

`new_project` can save the blank project at a path straight away, adding `.framejob` if the path lacks it. It won't use a path another open project holds, or one a window is still opening, and then nothing is created. Without a path the project stays an untitled draft. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

## Related

- [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/)
- [The Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/)
- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
- [Canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/)

---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The Welcome window is where you start when no project is open. It offers the ways in and your recent projects, and it takes dropped files.

  where={['Shown when Frame Job starts with nothing to open', 'Shown when you click the Dock icon with no window open']}

/>

/>

| Button | What it does |
| --- | --- |

| **New Recording…** | Opens the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/), with no project needed. |

## Reopen a recent project

Under the buttons, **Recent** lists up to five recently opened projects by name, most recent first. Click one to reopen it. Hover over a row to see its full path.

The window is a fixed 720 × 600 and can't be resized.

## Related

- [Start a project](/projects/start-a-project/)
- [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/)
- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)

## With an agent

`open_project` takes a path, absolute or starting with `~`, to a project, movie, sound file or picture. It differs from a person's open in two ways:

- It also recognises a movie already open as an untitled project, and brings that window forward instead of making a second one.
- It never asks the [ffmpeg question](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).

See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

title: New Project from Range
description: Keep one stretch of your timeline as a new project of its own, with its caches and graphics, and leave the original as it is.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

New Project from Range opens a new project holding exactly the timeline's In–Out range, moved to start at 0. Use it to lift a section out of a long edit to work on by itself. The project you made it from doesn't change.

<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ New Project from Range…" tools="new_project_from_range" />

## Make a project from a range

<Steps>

1. Set the [in/out range](/timeline/in-out-range/) with **Mark ▸ Set In** (<kbd>I</kbd>) and **Mark ▸ Set Out** (<kbd>O</kbd>).

2. Choose **File ▸ New Project from Range…**.

</Steps>

The new project opens in its own window straight away. There's no sheet to fill in, and the command has no key.

The item is off when no range is set, while a [nest](/editing/nests/) is open, and while a sheet is on the window.

## What is kept

- **Clips across an edge** are cut there, the same way [Split](/editing/splitting/) cuts them. This happens on every track, locked or not, and a linked pair stays linked.
- **Clips wholly inside the range** are kept. Everything outside it goes.
- **A transition across an edge** becomes a hard start or end. The piece beyond the edge is dropped, and at the In edge the incoming piece starts with no transition.
- **Markers inside the range** are kept and moved with the timeline. A marker exactly on the Out frame isn't kept.
- **Tracks and the canvas** stay as they are, including any track that ends up empty and any lock.
- **Media no kept clip plays** is left out, unless a kept clip still needs it as a look's [LUT](/color/luts/). Nests no kept clip reaches are left out too.

## What comes with it

The new project brings what's already been measured, so nothing is measured again when it opens. For each media file it keeps:

- filmstrips, waveforms, and loudness, speech and sync data
- transcripts read on this Mac
- [analyses](/projects/media-analysis/), such as shots, people's masks, faces, sound events and subjects
- the backwards render of a [reversed clip](/speed/reverse/)

Media files themselves are never copied. The new project points at the same files as the original.

[Speed ramp](/speed/speed-ramps/), [isolated voice](/audio/voice-isolation/) and [voice effect](/audio/voice-effects/) renders don't come along. They're made again when needed.

### Cloud transcripts

A transcript from [AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/) goes to the new project only once AssemblyAI has been told to delete its copy. One still waiting for that delete stays in the original project.

### Graphics

The graphics the kept clips draw come along, and so does every font and picture of the project's graphics, whether a kept clip uses it or not. A graphic's kept earlier versions don't.

## The new project's name and undo

The new project opens untitled with unsaved changes, named after its parent with " (range)" added, such as "Interview (range)". Closing it asks whether to save.

It starts at the range. There's no undo step back to the whole timeline, and the original project gets no undo step either, because nothing happened to it.

## When Frame Job won't do it

If the range can't be kept, the command beeps and shows why at the foot of the inspector, and no project opens.

| The message says | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| "Clip *N* is a nest across the range's edge; a nest clip has no in point, so a cut there would replay it from its start. Move the edge, or open the nest and unnest it." | Do one of those. A nest clip can't be cut at an edge. |
| "Nothing plays between …" | The range holds no clips. Move it over something. |
| A sentence naming two clips, ending "move an edge further from their transition." | An edge would cut a clip too short for a transition inside the range, leaving them overlapping by more than half of the shorter piece. Move the edge. |

The command also beeps when In and Out are on the same frame, because the range is empty.

## With an agent

`new_project_from_range` takes the range as times, so it doesn't need the In–Out range set. It can also save the new project at a path first, as long as nothing exists there and no other open project holds it. The assistant asks you before it does that. See [Tools: projects and history](/mcp/tools-projects/).

- [Make Vertical Version](/reframe/make-vertical/)

31	| Remove a marker | Choose **Delete** in its row in the Document tab. |
32	
33	Each of these is one undo step.
34	
35	Double-clicking a flag opens a field on the ruler. Return, Tab or a click elsewhere saves the name. <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the field and keeps the old name, and saving an empty field does nothing. 41	You can also choose **Go** in a marker's row in the Document tab.
42	
43	## The Markers list
44	
45	The **Markers** section of the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/) lists every marker in time order, with its time, its name, **Chapter**, **Go** and **Delete**. With no markers it reads "No markers. Press M to add one."
